conventions: TypeScript strict, ESM; Prettier 2.6 via @excalidraw/prettier-config (2-space indent, double quotes, trailing commas, 80-col wrap); eslint runs prettier as a rule, so formatting is a lint error.

Import groups separated by one blank line, in this order: external (react) / @excalidraw/* values / @excalidraw/* type imports / parent and sibling relative values / scss / relative types; type-only imports use a separate `import type` line (eslint import/order and consistent-type-imports, --max-warnings=0).

Across packages import through the @excalidraw/<pkg> alias (e.g. `@excalidraw/common`); inside a package use relative paths. Never import from the @excalidraw/excalidraw barrel inside packages/excalidraw source.
Exported helpers are `export const name = (...) => {...}` arrow functions; module-private helpers are plain `const`. Section dividers in colors.ts are `// ---...` comment lines.

Tests run on Vitest 3 with globals (describe/it/expect/vi, no imports for them), jsdom and vitest-canvas-mock (canvas pixels are not real). Assertions use expect(...).toBe / toMatch / toBeLessThanOrEqual; no new snapshots.
Integration tests render the full editor with `await render(<Excalidraw ... />)` from ./test-utils and read editor state through `const { h } = window;` (`h.state`, `h.app`).
Colour strings produced by code are lowercase `#rrggbb` built with `rgbToHex`; alpha is dropped where the eyedropper is concerned.
No new dependency; colour parsing uses tinycolor2 (already imported in colors.ts).
Do not change `applyDarkModeFilter`, `cssInvert` or `cssHueRotate` in colors.ts, and do not change or remove any existing test.

decisions.topic: Name and signature of the inverse helper
decisions.choice: `export const revertDarkModeFilter = (color: string, candidates: readonly string[] = []): string` in packages/common/src/colors.ts, reached through the existing `export * from "./colors"` of @excalidraw/common.
rejected: invertDarkModeFilter (confusable with the 93% css invert step)
a candidates-only lookup with no numeric fallback
decisions.reason: Reads as the opposite of applyDarkModeFilter, and FR-2 requires the numeric fallback for colours outside every candidate list.

decisions.choice: Caller candidates are tried first, in the order given, then the module's default candidates; the first candidate whose filtered colour matches wins.
decisions.reason: The filter is lossy, so two colours can share one on-screen pixel; the colours actually present in the scene are the better guess.

decisions.choice: Always a lowercase 6-digit `#rrggbb` (rgbToHex of the RGB channels), both for a candidate match and for the numeric fallback; an invalid input colour is returned unchanged.
decisions.reason: The eyedropper has always emitted 6-digit hex with no alpha, and palette colours are already lowercase 6-digit hex so they round-trip exactly.

decisions.choice: Apply the private cssHueRotate(r, g, b, 180 as Degrees) again (the 180 degree hue-rotate matrix is its own inverse), then invert the 93% css invert per channel with `(v - 255 * p) / (1 - 2 * p)` where p = 0.93, then Math.round(clamp(x, 0, 255)) and rgbToHex.
rejected: cssInvert(…, 93) a second time (not the inverse of a partial invert)
an iterative search over the 16M colour space
decisions.reason: Exact algebraic inverse of the two steps up to their rounding and clamping, constant cost per pixel.

decisions.topic: Where the scene candidates are built
decisions.choice: Inside EyeDropper.tsx getCurrentColor, only when the theme is dark: appState.viewBackgroundColor first, then every element's strokeColor and backgroundColor from useExcalidrawElements(), deduplicated with a Set, read at event time through the existing useStable object.
rejected: a useMemo in the component body
decisions.reason: Keeps the change inside getCurrentColor and the stable props, adds no file, and costs nothing in light theme (FR-5).

decisions.topic: How the reproducing test injects the pixel
decisions.choice: After the eyedropper is open, `vi.spyOn(h.app.canvas.getContext("2d")!, "getImageData").mockReturnValue({ data: new Uint8ClampedArray([r, g, b, 255]) } as unknown as ImageData)`; vitest-canvas-mock returns the same context object for every getContext("2d") call on a canvas, so EyeDropper's ctx is the spied one.
rejected: spying on CanvasRenderingContext2D.prototype (the mock binds methods per instance at construction)
decisions.reason: Targets exactly the context EyeDropper reads, with no global side effect on other tests.

units.behaviour: Reproduces the bug: in dark theme the eyedropper must store the colour that was rendered, not its dark-mode on-screen pixel, recovering off-palette scene colours through the scene candidates (FR-4); light theme keeps the raw pixel.
rules: 1. Add `import { applyDarkModeFilter, COLOR_PALETTE, THEME } from "@excalidraw/common";` as its own import group (blank line before and after) right after the react import, and `import { API } from "./helpers/api";` as the first line of the relative group, before the ./helpers/ui import.
2. After the existing imports add a blank line and `const { h } = window;`.
3. Append a new `describe("eye dropper in dark theme", () => { ... })` after the existing describe; do not touch the existing case.

4. Inside it define `const pickPixel = async (pixel: string) => { ... }`: Keyboard.keyPress("i"); await waitFor until `.excalidraw-eye-dropper-backdrop` exists in GlobalTestState.renderResult.container; spy as in the decision with r, g, b = parseInt(pixel.slice(1, 3), 16), parseInt(pixel.slice(3, 5), 16), parseInt(pixel.slice(5, 7), 16); fireEvent.pointerUp(backdrop, { clientX: 10, clientY: 10 }); then spy.mockRestore().

5. Every case renders `<Excalidraw autoFocus={true} handleKeyboardGlobally={true} theme={...} />` (plus initialData where stated) and asserts on `h.state.currentItemBackgroundColor` (the `i` eyedropper with nothing selected stores the picked colour there); its default is `transparent`, so no case can pass by accident.
6. Compute every expected and stubbed colour with applyDarkModeFilter at test time; hard-code no filtered hex.

7. The scene colours are exactly "#ff00ff" (element backgroundColor) and "#00ffff" (viewBackgroundColor): neither is in COLOR_PALETTE or any default pick list, and the numeric inverse misses them by 50 and 72 per channel, so only the scene candidates of FR-4 recover them. Never swap them for palette colours or mid-tones.

units.behaviour: Unit tests for revertDarkModeFilter: palette round-trip, candidate matching, alpha/case handling and the numeric fallback for mid-tones (saturated colours off every candidate list are lossy through the fallback, so they are recovered only as candidates and are never asserted on the fallback).
rules: 1. The @excalidraw/common import adds DEFAULT_CANVAS_BACKGROUND_PICKS and revertDarkModeFilter to the existing names, keeping one name per line in the existing order style.
2. Append `describe("revertDarkModeFilter", () => { ... })` between the applyDarkModeFilter describe and the rgbToHex describe; do not touch existing cases.

3. The palette list for the round-trip case is COLOR_PALETTE.black, COLOR_PALETTE.white and every shade of every array-valued COLOR_PALETTE entry (Object.values filtered with Array.isArray, flattened); `transparent` is excluded.
4. Use it.each over the palette list and over DEFAULT_CANVAS_BACKGROUND_PICKS so a failure names the colour.

5. The numeric-fallback case is an it.each over the mid-tones "#123456", "#abcdef" and "#7a6b5c" only (none is a default candidate); it compares channels by parsing the hex pairs with parseInt(…, 16) and asserts Math.abs(difference) toBeLessThanOrEqual(2) for each of r, g, b. Do not add saturated inputs (e.g. #ff00ff misses by 50 per channel): the fallback is lossy for them by design.

units.behaviour: Adds revertDarkModeFilter, which maps a dark-mode on-screen colour back to the colour rendered to produce it: exact match against candidate colours first, numeric inverse of the filter otherwise.
rules: 1. Insert after isOpaqueColor a new section (divider comment `// dark mode color reversal` framed by `// ---` lines like the other sections) holding a private const and the exported function; every constant it reads is declared above it, so no temporal-dead-zone access at module load.

2. Private `const DARK_MODE_DEFAULT_CANDIDATES: readonly string[] = Array.from(new Set([...]))` of COLOR_PALETTE.black, COLOR_PALETTE.white, every shade of every array-valued COLOR_PALETTE entry, and every entry of DEFAULT_ELEMENT_STROKE_PICKS, DEFAULT_ELEMENT_BACKGROUND_PICKS, BUCKET_FILL_BACKGROUND_PICKS and DEFAULT_CANVAS_BACKGROUND_PICKS.
3. revertDarkModeFilter: parse `color` with tinycolor; if not isValid() return `color` unchanged.
4. target = rgbToHex(r, g, b) of the parsed colour (alpha dropped, lowercase 6-digit).

5. For each candidate of `candidates` then DARK_MODE_DEFAULT_CANDIDATES: skip it when tinycolor says it is invalid or its alpha is 0; if applyDarkModeFilter(candidate).slice(0, 7) === target, return rgbToHex of the candidate's r, g, b.

6. Otherwise the numeric inverse of the decision: rotated = cssHueRotate(r, g, b, 180 as Degrees); each channel v becomes Math.round(clamp((v - 255 * p) / (1 - 2 * p), 0, 255)) with p = 0.93; return rgbToHex of the three.
7. Pure: no module state is written except what applyDarkModeFilter's own cache already does; no new import is needed (tinycolor, clamp, Degrees and cssHueRotate are already in the file).

8. A one-paragraph JSDoc above the function states the candidate order, the 6-digit return shape and that the numeric fallback is lossy: near-exact for mid-tones, but off by up to ~170 per channel for saturated colours (the 93% invert clamps them), which only an exact candidate recovers.

units.behaviour: getCurrentColor resolves the sampled pixel through revertDarkModeFilter with the scene's colours when the theme is dark, so preview, onChange and onSelect all get the rendered colour; light theme is unchanged.
rules: 1. The @excalidraw/common import becomes `import { EVENT, KEYS, THEME, revertDarkModeFilter, rgbToHex } from "@excalidraw/common";` (prettier wraps it).

2. useStable additionally receives `elements`, `theme: appState.theme` and `viewBackgroundColor: appState.viewBackgroundColor`, so getCurrentColor reads current values at event time without new effect dependencies.
3. getCurrentColor keeps the getImageData call unchanged and builds `const color = rgbToHex(pixel[0], pixel[1], pixel[2]);`.
4. If stableProps.theme !== THEME.DARK, return color (exactly today's result).

5. Otherwise build a Set<string> of stableProps.viewBackgroundColor, then each element's strokeColor and backgroundColor from stableProps.elements, and return revertDarkModeFilter(color, Array.from(set)).
6. Leave the effect's dependency array and every other line as they are.
